class.name: GFGDSceneTree
class.brief_description: Custom [SceneTree] that drives the GFGD framework and owns its startup order.
class.description: Entry point of the framework. Set [code]application/run/main_loop_type[/code] to [code]GFGDSceneTree[/code] to enable it; nothing else in GFGD runs without this. The startup order is fixed and worth knowing. The [GameplayTagsManager] is built first, so tag tables are loaded before any resource can reference a tag. Then the [GameInstance] is created from [code]application/game_framework/game_instance_script[/code] and its [code]_on_init[/code] is called. Level discovery and [GameMode] creation are deferred to the first processed frame, because the scene root only enters the tree after the main loop finishes initializing. How the level was opened decides when [code]GameMode._init_game[/code] runs relative to the level's nodes. [method open_level] instantiates the scene, creates the game mode and calls [code]_init_game[/code] while the level is still outside the scene tree, and only then adds it: every node is reachable and none has run [code]_enter_tree[/code] or [code]_ready[/code] yet. The first level is the exception. It is the main scene, which Godot adds before the framework gets control, so its nodes have already run [code]_ready[/code] when [code]_init_game[/code] is called. A project that wants the same ordering everywhere makes its main scene a menu or another level that does not need it, and reaches the real gameplay levels through [method open_level]. The [GameMode] node is added to the tree after the level in both cases, which makes its [code]_ready[/code] the point where the level, its nodes and the player are all live. [method Level._init_level] runs last.

method.name: create_default_local_player
method.description: Creates player 0 holding [constant PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_ALL] - every device drives it, which is what makes a project that never touches local multiplayer behave exactly as before. Called automatically when a game mode needs a player and none exists.

method.name: create_local_player
method.description: Adds a human at this machine, for the whole application rather than for this level. See [enum PlayerInput.DeviceSlot].

method.name: get_controllers
method.description: Every [Controller] in this world, AI controllers included.

method.name: get_first_player_controller
method.description: The first player in the world, or [code]null[/code] before anyone has been logged in and in a level whose game mode suppressed spawning. This lives on the world rather than on the [GameMode] because the game mode is the server's object and does not exist on a client, while this list does.

method.name: has_authority
method.description: True while there is no multiplayer peer, or while this peer is the server. The hook exists so server-only code - anything on the [GameMode] - can be written now and stay correct once there is networking.

method.name: register_controller
method.description: Controllers call this themselves from [code]_enter_tree[/code]. It is idempotent, so a game mode may register one eagerly before it enters the tree.

method.name: open_level
method.description: Frees the current level, [GameMode] and [GameState] and builds the new one. Every [LocalPlayer] survives and is logged in again, so device assignment carries across.
